episodes.title: The Calendar Decision: Should a CFO Elect Semiannual Reporting?
episodes.subtitle: SEC File No. S7-2026-15, a 97 percent comment-file revolt, and the board posture that will not wait
episodes.description: An HBS-style case set on 1 September 2026. After the SEC proposed letting U.S. public companies replace Form 10-Q with a semiannual Form 10-S, and after a historically lopsided comment file closed 97 percent opposed, a mid-cap industrial CFO must recommend whether her board should pre-commit to quarterly reporting, prepare to elect, wait for a first cohort, or set a liquidity trigger. Real Commission statements, comment statistics, and CFA survey findings are woven through a teaching composite so students decide.

episodes.title: AI ROI Blind Spot: Protiviti Survey
episodes.subtitle: Why many finance leaders still struggle to measure returns on AI investments
episodes.description: A recent Protiviti survey highlights a critical blind spot: while organisations continue to invest heavily in AI, many CFOs and finance teams still lack clear frameworks to measure and report AI returns. This episode helps students understand how future finance leaders should approach AI investment decisions, measurement, and governance.

episodes.title: AI ROI Paradox in Finance
episodes.subtitle: When heavy AI investment meets uncertain returns — what should a CFO do?
episodes.description: Today’s episode examines the growing paradox facing finance leaders: significant investment in AI tools and infrastructure is being made, yet clear, measurable returns remain elusive for many organisations. Students learn how a CFO should evaluate AI spend, measure value, and decide when to scale or pause.

episodes.title: The $3.2 Trillion Question Hiding in Plain Sight
episodes.subtitle: NVIDIA’s Record Quarter and the Off-Balance-Sheet AI Infrastructure Commitments of the AI-7
episodes.description: NVIDIA reported record Q2 FY2027 results while research revealed that the AI-7 companies now carry approximately $3.2 trillion in contractual commitments largely sitting in footnotes. This episode teaches students how to read true committed capital, utilisation risk, and the difference between reported leverage and reality.
